question.text: Vidarbha Infra Fund values investee Konkan Ports on replacement cost basis. Book value of assets = INR 200 crore; appreciation in inventory and intangibles = INR 10 crore; additional setup/licensing costs to recreate business = INR 30 crore; depreciation in fixed assets on going-concern basis = INR 15 crore. Replacement value is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Illustration 11.4 Part III: Replacement Value = Book Value + Appreciation (inventory/intangibles) + Setup Costs - Fixed Asset Dep on going-concern = 200 + 10 + 30 - 15 = INR 225 crore. This is Enterprise Value on replacement basis. The Trap: INR 200 is plain book; INR 230 forgets the dep haircut; INR 245 double-counts setup costs. Replacement cost = what it would cost a new entrant to BUILD this business today. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests identical logic. Series-XV (Research Analyst) tests replacement cost for asset-heavy sectors (cement, infra) where it often dominates DCF. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cat I/II infra AIFs often anchor bids on replacement cost for brownfield assets because the DCF is too sensitive to tariff assumptions. Disclose the 'Tobin's Q' (market value / replacement cost) ratio in your IC deck to show whether you're paying a greenfield premium.
